string.text: Gunpowder Ba-10 "Falcon"

The most widespread and affordable gunpowder in the Zone. Originally produced in mass quantities for Soviet and NATO law enforcement, these can be found in almost every rookie's stash, bandit camp, or trader's bunker. It burns quickly and reliably in short pistol barrels, making it the default choice for reloading 9x18mm and 9x19mm rounds. While it lacks high stopping power, its sheer abundance makes it the backbone of Zone self-defense.
Gunpowder 206SV "Hawk"

The standard propellant for automatic and assault rifles across the Zone. It is balanced to provide sustained, stable gas pressure during rapid or fully automatic fire. It is heavily utilized by Stalkers to reload empty casings for AK-pattern and Western assault rifles. While it doesn't offer the extreme accuracy of sniper blends, its high thermal tolerance prevents catastrophic cook-offs during intense firefights.
Gunpowder A1-SP "Korshun"

Standard soviet or domestic smokeless gunpowder. Due to the Zone's high humidity, it often becomes damp, leading to misfires at the worst possible moments. Experienced stalkers use it to hand-load shotgun shells and slugs. It is cheap and readily available but requires drying before use.
Gunpowder C7L "Raven"

Specialized fast-burning gunpowder designed for heavy, large-caliber handgun ammunition. Sourced primarily from mercenary stashes or smuggled Western military supplies. It generates massive chamber pressure, allowing heavy bullets to stop an aggressive mutant in its tracks. However, it fouls weapon barrels quickly and causes severe recoil. Highly valued by owners of heavy revolvers.
Gunpowder Tu500 "Berkut"

High-grade, slow-burning military gunpowder meant for long-range, large-caliber sniper rifles. Unlike standard rifle powder, its granules are chemically coated to ensure perfectly uniform combustion, minimizing shot variance at extreme distances. Due to its strict storage requirements, uncompromised tins can only be found in deep military caches or Pripyat stashes.

Center punches

A heavy, crudely fashioned tool-steel center punch featuring a reinforced titanium tip and a depth stop. It is a makeshift device, yet extremely popular within the Zone. It allows for the field modification of standard military full metal jacket (FMJ) rounds. With a single precise, forceful strike to the bullet's nose, the punch neatly deforms the jacket and creates a hollow cavity, effectively converting a standard round into a hollow-point (HP) cartridge. The powerful internal cocking mechanism deforms after the very first use, causing the tool to quickly dull and become unusable.
Incendiary powder

A jar of a volatile, finely ground pyrotechnic mixture based on barium nitrate, magnesium powder. In laboratory conditions, this compound is pressed into the rear cavities of bullets to create tracer ammunition.
Rosin solder

A bundle of thin, consumable steel welding electrodes with a hollow core filled with natural pine rosin. Originally meant for low-temperature civilian metalwork, these rods have become a staple in every stalker technician’s toolkit across the Zone. The integrated rosin acts as a built-in flux, cleaning oxide films from rusted metal surfaces during heating. Used for hardening cheap bullets..
Diluted powder

A pouch containing a specialized, fine-grained chemical compound consisting of inert fillers, burning rate stabilizers, and a pinch of ground sulfur. Developed by desperate stalker-craftsmen during periods of severe supply shortages, this powder is used to increase the volume of high-quality military gunpowder.
Lead weights

A heavy jar containing soft, malleable lead weights with a high content of bismuth and tin, drastically lowering their melting point. Originally manufactured for civilian fishing nets and diving belts, these weights have become a highly sought-after commodity among the Zone’s handcrafters and gunsmiths.
